summary: Iteration 39 - Verified premade-courses inline viewing (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, TXT) and audio TTS browser-fallback. Backend: 9/9 pytest cases pass. Frontend: all 4 document types render in the correct viewer (react-pdf canvas, docx-preview, LibreOffice-converted PDF canvas), no download links anywhere, 'View Only' badge + 'Downloading, copying and printing are disabled' footer present. Audio TTS fallback proved: backend /api/advanced/tts returned 503 (LLM budget exceeded), code path automatically called window.speechSynthesis.speak() with the lesson text, button flipped to 'Pause' state, and the 'Failed to generate audio' toast was NOT shown.

critical.issue: Still returns 503 due to Emergent LLM key budget exceeded. The frontend now handles this gracefully via browser-TTS fallback so this is no longer a user-blocking issue, but cloud-quality TTS is still unavailable until the key budget is refilled.

issues: React warning: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby for DialogContent'. Cosmetic a11y warning only.

action_items: (Optional, low-priority) Add DialogDescription / aria-describedby to PremadeCoursesPage view dialog to clear the React a11y warning.
(Environmental) Refill the Emergent LLM key budget so cloud TTS works again. Browser-TTS fallback masks this from end users but cloud voices are still nicer.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend /api/premade-courses/{doc_id}/view is well structured: PDF / images / TXT / DOCX served as-is, legacy Office formats converted to PDF via LibreOffice on-demand and cached at /app/generated_pdf_cache/. soffice binary path is dynamically resolved with sensible fallback.
Frontend speakWithBrowserTTS picks higher-quality voice when available (Google/Natural/Samantha/Microsoft) before falling back to the default English voice — good polish.
handleGenerateAudio detects /budget|quota/ in the backend error and shows a different toast ('Cloud audio quota reached — using browser voice instead.') — graceful UX.
playAudio correctly handles both cloud (HTMLAudioElement) and browser (speechSynthesis pause/resume) paths.
PremadeCoursesPage uses local /pdf.worker.min.mjs (verified, 1MB present) so react-pdf does not hit a CDN; good for offline/airgapped deployments.
View dialog shows 'View Only' badge and 'This document is view-only. Downloading, copying and printing are disabled.' footer; matches the spec's 'no download links anywhere' requirement.
Minor: a11y warning 'Missing Description or aria-describedby for DialogContent' — should add a hidden DialogDescription element.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 4 premade-courses doc types rendered correctly + audio fallback verified end-to-end)

test_credentials: Teacher demo.teacher@eduos.edu/demo123 and Student demo.student@cognify.edu/demo123 both working.
seed_data_creation: Test relies on existing premade-courses (PPTX Test, DOCX Conversion Test, AU NOTES 2026.pdf, premade_test.txt). Test fixtures upload synthetic PDF/DOCX/PPTX if absent.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All iteration-39 fixes are working as designed. Premade-courses /view endpoint serves correct MIME types (application/pdf inline for pdf+converted office, wordprocessingml for docx, original for txt/images). Frontend uses react-pdf for PDFs (canvas), docx-preview for DOCX (preserves Word styling), and react-pdf again for converted office docs. Audio mode: backend 503 → browser TTS fallback triggers, UI shows 'Pause', no error toast. The pause/resume programmatic verification could not assert paused=True because in headless Chromium speechSynthesis.speak does not actually start without an audio device — but the UI button transitions ('Generate Audio' → 'Pause' → 'Play Audio') were verified visually.
rca of the issue: User complaint 1 (documents not in original format) RCA: previous implementation extracted text from documents. New implementation streams raw bytes for PDF/DOCX and uses LibreOffice headless conversion for legacy Office formats, then renders client-side (react-pdf / docx-preview). User complaint 2 ('Failed to generate audio') RCA: backend /api/advanced/tts intermittently returns 503 (Emergent LLM key budget exceeded). Fix: handleGenerateAudio now wraps the cloud call in a try/catch and on failure invokes window.speechSynthesis.speak() with the full lesson text; audioPlaying state hooks to utter.onstart/onend so the UI flips to 'Pause' correctly. Verified live: backend returned 503 during test, browser-TTS fallback executed, button changed to 'Pause', no failure toast surfaced to user.
